title: Small-balance commercial real estate (CRE) debt brokerage — Chicago-area investors and owner-users
subindustry: Commercial mortgage brokerage (5+ unit multifamily, mixed-use, retail/industrial, owner-occupied CRE; ~$0.5M-$5M loans)
product_service: Placement of acquisition/refinance/bridge debt for small CRE with banks, credit unions, debt funds, life-co/agency small-balance programs; prepare loan package, run lender competition, manage to close.
target_customer: Private real-estate investors and owner-users (dentists, manufacturers, contractors) holding or buying $0.5M-$5M properties in Chicagoland; also small sponsors.
purchase_motivation: Better terms/leverage, speed, access to non-bank lenders when their own bank declines; refinancing walls on 2019-2021 vintage loans.
spending_evidence: Large incumbents earn ~83 bps origination fees on debt financing volume, 54% of it brokered [B, WS01-S035]; Illinois has 279 loan-broker establishments (NAICS 522310) [C, WS01-S021]. Small-balance fee levels for Chicago not sourced.
representative_operators: Walker & Dunlop — national CRE finance incumbent; $647M Capital Markets revenue 2025 [B, WS01-S035]
Local Chicago CRE mortgage brokers — names not verified in this session [E]
revenue_mechanism: Borrower-paid success fee (commonly ~0.5-2% of loan, unverified) and/or lender-paid points; paid at closing.
typical_transaction_value: $1.5M loan x ~1% = ~$15,000 fee per close [E]; 1-2 closes/month plausible for an established solo broker [E]
direct_costs: Producer splits if hiring (often 50-70% of fee to producer, unverified), data subscriptions, E&O insurance, travel, third-party report deposits (pass-through).
contribution_profit_note: Solo founder: ~85-90% of fee is contribution; with commissioned producers ~30-50% to house [E].
working_capital_note: No inventory or receivables; fees paid at closing. Founder must self-fund 4-9 months of living costs before first close.
sales_cycle: 60-150 days from engagement to close; relationship trust built over multiple conversations.
repeat_purchase: occasional — investors refinance/acquire every 1-5 years; good clients repeat and refer.
acquisition_channels: Cook/collar-county recorder & assessor data on maturing loans and recent buyers
Commercial real estate sales brokers and property managers
Local REIA and CRE association events
customer_accessibility: Owners identifiable from public property records; winning engagements requires credibility (track record, lender relationships) that a new entrant lacks.
supplier_accessibility: Assumed: community banks, credit unions and debt funds accept broker submissions; many smaller banks do not pay broker fees (borrower pays). Not verified.
competitive_intensity: high — established CRE advisors, bank relationship managers, online marketplaces.
entry_strategy: Pick a narrow asset type (e.g., 5-49 unit multifamily or industrial condos) and a lender panel; offer speed and complete packages; partner with a senior CRE banker as advisor/co-broker.
licenses: Illinois RMLA does not apply to entities solely in commercial mortgage lending; 5+ unit multifamily is not a 'dwelling' (1-4 units) [A, WS01-S004, WS01-S005]. Illinois Loan Brokers Act (815 ILCS 175): exempt from Secretary of State registration only if the fee is wholly contingent on successful procurement (binding commitment) apart from bona fide third-party fees; burden of proof on broker [A, WS01-S002]. Non-exempt brokers register with SOS; $25k bond only for TILA (consumer) loans [A, WS01-S003]. Real estate broker license not needed for debt placement (not verified for sale-side fees). Out-of-state borrowers: California requires a CFL broker license for more than bare referrals on commercial loans [A, WS01-S017, WS01-S018]; New York treats brokers presenting offers as 'providers' with disclosure duties for deals <= $2.5M (real-estate-secured and true leases exempt) [A, WS01-S015, WS01-S016]; Texas requires OCCC registration of sales-based-financing brokers by 2026-12-31 [A, WS01-S014]. Other states with commercial-financing disclosure laws not verified in this session.
regulatory_barriers: Low in Illinois if success-fee only; any upfront 'due diligence' fee triggers SOS registration and advance-fee scrutiny.
operational_risks: Deals die late (appraisal, rate moves); borrower circumvention (going direct to lender); reputation damage from failed closes.
financial_risks: Lumpy income; zero revenue in CRE downturns; long ramp funded by founder.
geographic_constraints: Relationship business best done locally; lender panels national.
founder_expertise: CRE underwriting (NOI, DSCR, cap rates), lender appetites, term-sheet negotiation; 6-12 months of learning.
staffing: Solo first 12-18 months; then analyst/processor; later commissioned producers.
automation_potential: AI/software: rent-roll and T-12 spreading, offering memo drafting, lender matching database, outreach list building from public records. Human: trust, negotiation, deal rescue.
delegation_potential: Producers can be hired but tend to own relationships and leave; analyst/processing functions delegable.
scalability: People-scaled; a 3-5 producer shop is a common ceiling for local brokers [E].
expansion: Equity placement, sale-side brokerage (requires real estate license), loan servicing for private lenders, own-capital bridge lending later.
roic_note: Capital at risk ~$5-15k plus founder ramp time; ratio is high if it works, but probability of reaching $100k/yr in 3 years for an unknown entrant is uncertain [E].
critical_assumptions: Borrowers will pay ~1% success fees to a new broker
Lenders accept submissions from unproven brokers
unanswered_questions: Typical small-balance CRE broker fee in Chicago (bps) — MISSING
Share of community banks that pay broker fees — MISSING
Average close rate of broker engagements — MISSING
failure_modes: Never builds lender relationships or track record
Deals lost to borrower's own bank
score_rationale: fcf 5: solo brokers plausibly reach ~$100-150k but unproven [E]. access 4: owners findable but credibility wall. entry 3: crowded with no inherent wedge. cash 8: paid at close, no WC. feasibility 8: no Illinois license if success-fee only.
preliminary_verdict: hold — legally clean and asset-light, but crowded and credibility-gated; better as an adjacency to a niche lending model than as the first business.

title: Generalist small-business loan brokerage via lender referral/ISO programs
subindustry: Commercial loan brokerage (term loans, lines of credit, SBA referrals, equipment) for Main Street SMBs
product_service: Match small businesses to online lenders, banks and SBA lenders through partner programs; help assemble applications; earn lender-paid commission on funded deals.
target_customer: Owner-operators of SMBs with $250k-$5M revenue seeking $25k-$500k.
purchase_motivation: Working capital, expansion, equipment, refinancing expensive debt; owners lack time/knowledge to shop lenders.
spending_evidence: 38% of employer firms applied for a loan/LOC/MCA in the prior year; 22% of applicants received nothing [C, WS01-S031]. US NAICS 522310 had $18.3B receipts in 2022 (mortgage + nonmortgage) [C, WS01-S022].
representative_operators: SmartBiz Bank — publishes 2% referral commission on funded loans, SBA 7(a) $50k-$350k [B, WS01-S029]
Lendio — marketplace; franchise page returns 404 (2026-11-28) [D, WS01-S028]
National Funding — broker program 'at full capacity' [D, WS01-S026]
revenue_mechanism: Lender-paid commission on funded amount (e.g., 2% of funded SBA/term loans at SmartBiz [B, WS01-S029]); online-lender commissions vary and are mostly unpublished.
typical_transaction_value: $150k SBA 7(a) x 2% = $3,000 per funded deal [B, WS01-S029]; smaller online term loans likely lower absolute dollars [E]
direct_costs: Paid lead acquisition (cost per lead MISSING), CRM/data, sub-ISO or rep splits.
contribution_profit_note: If lead cost is $X and funded rate is low (often <20% of raw leads, unverified), contribution per funded deal can be thin; organic/referral channels far better [E].
working_capital_note: Commission paid ~10-15 days after funding at SmartBiz [B, WS01-S029]; paid-lead spend is upfront.
sales_cycle: 2-8 weeks for online/term loans; 45-90 days SBA.
repeat_purchase: occasional — renewals and new needs every 1-3 years; some lender programs pay on renewals (unverified).
acquisition_channels: Outbound to businesses with public signals (permits, UCC filings)
customer_accessibility: Many buyers actively seek financing; but they search online and land on large marketplaces first.
supplier_accessibility: Confirmed: lender partner programs exist and publish sign-up (SmartBiz, Credibly, OnDeck, Biz2Credit) [B/D, WS01-S029, WS01-S041]; some at capacity [D, WS01-S026].
competitive_intensity: extreme — national marketplaces (Lendio, NerdWallet), lender direct marketing, thousands of ISOs.
entry_strategy: Become the financing desk for a referral network (CPAs, bookkeepers, business brokers) rather than buying leads; specialize later.
licenses: Illinois Loan Brokers Act (815 ILCS 175): exempt from Secretary of State registration only if the fee is wholly contingent on successful procurement (binding commitment) apart from bona fide third-party fees; burden of proof on broker [A, WS01-S002]. Non-exempt brokers register with SOS; $25k bond only for TILA (consumer) loans [A, WS01-S003]. Lender-paid success commissions fit the contingency exemption. SBA referrals require SBA Form 159 disclosure by the lender [A, WS01-S013]. Out-of-state borrowers: California requires a CFL broker license for more than bare referrals on commercial loans [A, WS01-S017, WS01-S018]; New York treats brokers presenting offers as 'providers' with disclosure duties for deals <= $2.5M (real-estate-secured and true leases exempt) [A, WS01-S015, WS01-S016]; Texas requires OCCC registration of sales-based-financing brokers by 2026-12-31 [A, WS01-S014]. Other states with commercial-financing disclosure laws not verified in this session.
regulatory_barriers: Low in Illinois; rising disclosure/registration burden in NY, CA, TX and other states if serving national clients.
operational_risks: Low approval rates on thin files; fraud by applicants (doctored bank statements) harming lender relationships.
financial_risks: Lead spend without fundings; possible commission clawbacks on early default/prepayment (terms MISSING).
geographic_constraints: National via phone/online; licensing limits in CA etc.
founder_expertise: Credit basics, lender product boxes, SBA eligibility; 2-4 months.
staffing: Solo, then loan coordinators/processors; commissioned reps.
automation_potential: AI: bank-statement analysis, eligibility pre-screen, lender matching, document collection follow-up. Human: trust-building, partner management.
delegation_potential: Processing delegable; origination relationships are personal.
scalability: Moderate; scaling usually means buying leads (margin pressure) or building partner networks.
expansion: Niche verticals (WS01-003, WS01-018), equipment finance, factoring referrals.
roic_note: Asset-light; capital mostly for lead tests. ROIC high only if organic referral flow develops.
critical_assumptions: Referral partners (CPAs) will send clients to a new broker
unanswered_questions: Lead cost per funded deal in business lending — MISSING
Commission clawback terms in non-MCA lender agreements — MISSING
Why Lendio franchise page is gone and what franchisee economics were — MISSING
failure_modes: Buying leads that do not fund
Drifting into MCA to make volume
score_rationale: entry 2: commodity with entrenched marketplaces. fcf 4: $3k-type commissions need ~40+ funded deals/yr for $100k. cash 8: lender pays within weeks. feasibility 8: IL contingency exemption.
preliminary_verdict: hold — legal and cheap to test but commoditized; only interesting as a channel inside a niche model.

title: Business-acquisition financing advisory for first-time buyers and search funds (SBA 7(a) change-of-ownership loans)
product_service: Package acquisition loans (deal model, projections, SBA eligibility/equity-injection and seller-note structuring), shop 7(a) lenders, coordinate to close; fee paid by buyer for packaging and/or lender referral fee, disclosed on SBA Form 159.
target_customer: Individual buyers and self-funded/traditional searchers acquiring $1M-$8M-price small businesses; their business brokers and attorneys.
purchase_motivation: Buyers are first-timers with one shot at a deal; lender fit and speed determine whether the acquisition happens.
spending_evidence: SOP 50 10 8.1 explicitly regulates agent packaging and referral fees, implying an established paid agent market [A, WS01-S013]; SmartBiz pays 2% referral on SBA loans <= $350k [B, WS01-S029]. Acquisition-loan volume data not retrieved.
representative_operators: Specialist SBA acquisition-loan advisors exist (names not verified this session) [E]
SBA 7(a) lenders' own BDO teams compete directly [E]
revenue_mechanism: Applicant-paid packaging fee (hourly or % basis; % basis capped at 2% to $1M + 0.25% above, $30k aggregate; must NOT be contingent on approval) plus lender-paid referral fee (separate service, disclosed) [A, WS01-S013, WS01-S012].
typical_transaction_value: $2M loan: applicant packaging fee legally capped at $22,500 on % basis [A, WS01-S013]; realistic $7.5k-$15k packaging + possible lender referral fee (amount unpublished) [E]
direct_costs: Analyst time, financial-model tools, E&O insurance, Illinois SOS loan-broker registration (non-contingent fees).
contribution_profit_note: ~$10-25k per closed deal before overhead if both fee streams apply [E].
working_capital_note: Non-contingent packaging fees can be billed in stages (engagement, submission); lender referral at closing.
sales_cycle: Buyer engagement to close 60-120 days; many LOIs fail (deal mortality high, unverified).
repeat_purchase: none-to-occasional per buyer; repeat comes from business brokers and searcher communities referring multiple buyers.
customer_accessibility: Buyers are self-identifying and actively searching for financing; business brokers want financeable buyers.
supplier_accessibility: Assumed: many 7(a) lenders accept agent-referred acquisition deals; referral-fee willingness varies (unverified).
competitive_intensity: moderate — specialized niche, but lenders' BDOs and established advisors compete.
entry_strategy: Be the fastest, most rigorous packager (lender-ready credit memo, QoE-lite analysis) with transparent SBA-compliant fees; build business-broker referral network.
licenses: SBA: Agent rules (13 CFR 103), Form 159 for all agents not under LSP agreement; fee caps and no contingency fees charged to applicants [A, WS01-S012, WS01-S013]. Illinois: because SBA forbids contingent applicant fees, an applicant-paid packager likely loses the Loan Brokers Act contingency exemption and must register with the Secretary of State (TILA bond not needed for business loans) [A, WS01-S002, WS01-S003] — analyst reading, confirm with counsel.
regulatory_barriers: SBA can suspend/revoke agent privileges for unreasonable fees or undisclosed relationships [A, WS01-S012]; conflict between SBA non-contingency rule and Illinois exemption structure needs legal review.
operational_risks: Deal mortality (seller issues, QoE surprises); reputational risk if buyer overpays and defaults.
financial_risks: Lumpy; acquisition market rate-sensitive; non-contingent fee model may lower close rate of engagements.
geographic_constraints: National (SBA program); CA CFL licensing if packaging for CA borrowers may apply.
founder_expertise: SBA SOP (eligibility, equity injection, seller notes, change of ownership), small-business valuation, credit analysis; 3-6 months focused study.
staffing: Founder + analyst by year 2; possibly ex-SBA underwriter advisor.
automation_potential: AI: CIM/tax-return spreading, DSCR models, SBA forms, eligibility checklists, credit memo drafting — material time savings. Human: deal judgment, lender/broker relationships.
delegation_potential: Analyst/packager roles delegable with SOPs after ~2 years; founder remains rainmaker early.
scalability: National niche; team of 3-6 packagers plausible; ceiling tied to acquisition market volume.
expansion: Post-close services (bookkeeping, SBA servicing support), equity/seller-note placement, buyer-side diligence services.
roic_note: Capital at risk <$15k; returns dominated by founder time; high ratio if 12-25 closes/yr achieved [E].
critical_assumptions: Buyers will pay non-contingent packaging fees
Lenders pay referral fees on acquisition loans
unanswered_questions: SBA 7(a) change-of-ownership loan count/volume FY2025-26 — MISSING
Typical lender referral fees on $1M+ 7(a) loans — MISSING
Illinois SOS registration fee and whether IDFPR/SOS views SBA packagers as loan brokers — MISSING
failure_modes: High deal mortality with unpaid work
SBA policy swings (equity injection, seller-note rules) shrinking eligible deals
Competing against lender BDOs who are free to the buyer
score_rationale: access 6: buyers self-identify and business brokers refer. entry 5: real wedge (acquisition-specific expertise) but copyable. feasibility 7: SOS registration + SBA agent compliance, no license exam. ai 6: heavy document/financial analysis work.
preliminary_verdict: advance — reachable, self-identifying buyers, high ticket and explicit fee rules; deep-dive on volume, referral fees and Illinois registration.

title: SBA 7(a)/504 packaging for established SMBs buying owner-occupied real estate or expanding (CPA-channel)
subindustry: SBA loan packaging (applicant-paid) and lender/CDC referral
product_service: Prepare SBA 7(a)/504 applications (business plan, projections, forms), coordinate bank + CDC for 504 owner-occupied real estate/equipment; fee from applicant (non-contingent) and/or referral fee from lender/CDC, disclosed on Form 159.
target_customer: Established profitable SMBs ($1M-$20M revenue) buying their building or major equipment; reached via their CPAs.
purchase_motivation: Owning real estate, long-term fixed financing, low down payment; owners lack time to manage two-lender 504 process.
spending_evidence: SOP 50 10 8.1 sets agent fee rules for 7(a) and 504, including CDC referral fees for third-party financing [A, WS01-S013]. Volume of agent-assisted loans MISSING.
representative_operators: CDCs and SBA lenders themselves package for free (competition) [E]
Independent SBA packaging consultants (not verified) [E]
revenue_mechanism: Hourly or % packaging fee (caps per SOP), plus referral fees from lender or CDC where permitted and disclosed [A, WS01-S013].
typical_transaction_value: $1.5M 504 project: packaging fee $5k-$15k (cap 2% to $1M + 0.25% above = $21,250) [A/E, WS01-S013]
direct_costs: Labor, E&O, SOS registration if non-contingent fees.
contribution_profit_note: ~$5-15k per closed project [E].
working_capital_note: Staged non-contingent billing; no inventory.
repeat_purchase: occasional — owners do 1-3 such projects per decade; CPAs refer repeatedly.
customer_accessibility: Reachable via CPAs but owners often go straight to their bank, which packages for free.
supplier_accessibility: CDCs and 7(a) lenders accept packaged deals; referral fee willingness varies (unverified).
competitive_intensity: moderate-high — banks/CDCs provide the same service at no explicit cost.
entry_strategy: White-label 'SBA desk' for CPA firms; value is reducing CPA and owner time.
licenses: Same as WS01-003: SBA agent rules/Form 159 and fee caps [A, WS01-S012, WS01-S013]; Illinois SOS loan-broker registration likely if fees are non-contingent [A, WS01-S002, WS01-S003].
regulatory_barriers: SBA agent oversight; prohibition on charging for the same service twice and on lender pass-through of LSP fees [A, WS01-S013].
operational_risks: Unpaid work on deals that never apply; owner indecision.
financial_risks: Real estate cycles; SBA program changes.
geographic_constraints: Local CPA relationships matter; program is national.
founder_expertise: SBA 504/7(a) mechanics, CRE basics, financial projections.
automation_potential: AI drafting of business plans/projections and SBA forms; human for owner/CPA relationships.
delegation_potential: Packaging delegable; referral relationships founder-led early.
scalability: Limited by how many owners will pay for what banks give free.
expansion: Pairs with WS01-003 and WS01-005 (lender-side services).
roic_note: Asset-light; returns depend on paid-engagement volume.
critical_assumptions: Owners pay for packaging despite free bank help
unanswered_questions: Share of SBA loans with paid agents (Form 159 data) — MISSING
CDC referral fee norms — MISSING
failure_modes: Too few projects per CPA relationship
score_rationale: entry 3: free substitutes (bank/CDC packaging). access 4: depends on CPA gatekeepers. Distinct from WS01-003 because buyers are established owners and the substitute is their own bank.
preliminary_verdict: reject as standalone — weaker than WS01-003 because banks/CDCs package for free; keep as add-on service.

title: Outsourced SBA loan processing, closing and Lender Service Provider (LSP) services for community banks and credit unions
subindustry: SBA 7(a) LSP / outsourced packaging-processing for lenders
product_service: Under an SBA-reviewed LSP agreement (or lender-paid agent engagement), perform eligibility review, credit memo drafting, E-Tran submission, closing checklists, servicing/1502 support for lenders lacking SBA staff.
target_customer: Community banks (<$1B) and credit unions wanting SBA volume without an SBA department; new/expanding non-bank SBA lenders.
purchase_motivation: SBA guaranty and secondary-market premiums are attractive but SBA compliance is specialized; staffing a department is costly.
spending_evidence: SOP 50 10 8.1 formalizes LSP agreements and states lender may contract third parties for SBA functions [A, WS01-S013]; 267 Illinois FDIC banks <= $1B assets [A, WS01-S039]. LSP pricing data MISSING.
representative_operators: SBA LSP firms exist nationally (names not verified this session) [E]
Technology-enabled underwriting vendors are treated as LSPs per SOP [A, WS01-S013]
revenue_mechanism: Per-loan fees and/or bps of loan amount paid by lender (not passable to borrower); possibly servicing fees; no sharing of secondary-market premiums allowed [A, WS01-S012, WS01-S013].
typical_transaction_value: Per-loan processing fee — MISSING (guess $2k-$8k per loan [E])
direct_costs: Experienced SBA underwriter/closer salaries (scarce), E&O, cyber/SOC2-type controls lenders require.
contribution_profit_note: Labor-based; margin depends on utilization of expensive SBA staff [E].
working_capital_note: Net-30 B2B invoices; payroll before revenue for specialist hires.
sales_cycle: 3-12 months (bank vendor due diligence, board approval, SBA review of LSP agreement).
repeat_purchase: recurring-contract — per-loan flow under multi-year LSP agreements.
acquisition_channels: State bankers and credit union leagues
customer_accessibility: Lenders are identifiable (FDIC/NCUA data) but conservative; vendor management and references required.
supplier_accessibility: N/A (service); key input is hiring experienced SBA staff — assumed scarce.
competitive_intensity: moderate — established LSPs and SBA consultants.
entry_strategy: Credit-union focus (many lack SBA programs), AI-assisted turnaround, pay-per-loan pricing.
licenses: No state license for commercial loan services; SBA LSP agreement review required and lender remains responsible; LSP fees cannot be charged to applicants [A, WS01-S012, WS01-S013]. Agents must be U.S.-located [A, WS01-S013].
regulatory_barriers: SBA OCRM oversight; bank third-party risk management expectations.
operational_risks: Errors cause guaranty repair/denial — lender losses and liability; key-person dependence on SBA expert hires.
financial_risks: Pre-revenue payroll; concentration on few lender clients.
founder_expertise: Deep SBA SOP knowledge — founder cannot supply initially; must hire or partner with a veteran SBA credit officer.
staffing: SBA underwriter/closer at launch (market salary), then processors.
automation_potential: High: eligibility checks, document intake, credit memo drafting, E-Tran data prep, closing checklists. Human: credit judgment, lender relationship, quality control.
scalability: National multi-lender; per-loan unit economics repeatable.
expansion: Loan review (WS01-028), servicing/liquidation support, 504 CDC services.
roic_note: $50-100k payroll at risk before contracts; moderate ROIC [E].
critical_assumptions: Lenders will outsource to a new firm
Can hire an SBA veteran on equity/profit share
unanswered_questions: LSP market pricing per loan — MISSING
Number of credit unions in IL with SBA programs — MISSING
SBA LSP agreement review timeline — MISSING
failure_modes: Guaranty purchase denials traced to LSP errors
score_rationale: access 3: bank vendor walls. ai 7: document-heavy compliance work suits AI. feasibility 6: no license but founder lacks required expertise; must hire.
preliminary_verdict: hold — attractive B2B recurring model with real AI leverage, but founder lacks SBA credibility; viable only with an experienced SBA partner.

representative_operators: Credibly — funder with broker/referral programs [D, WS01-S041]
National Funding — broker program at capacity [D, WS01-S026]
revenue_mechanism: Points on funded advance paid by funder (commonly reported as high single to double digits, NOT verified here) plus renewal commissions; clawbacks on early default typical (unverified).
typical_transaction_value: MISSING — commission levels not published by funders reviewed [D, WS01-S041]
direct_costs: Leads (UCC lists, aged leads, calling), sales reps on commission, compliance.
contribution_profit_note: MISSING — economics depend on unpublished commission and clawback terms.

unanswered_questions: Primary FTC/NY AG enforcement records against MCA brokers (not retrievable: web search budget exhausted) — MISSING
Published ISO commission and clawback schedules — MISSING

preliminary_verdict: reject — economics rely on high-cost renewals/stacking to distressed merchants; adverse regulatory trend and enforcement risk.

title: Equipment finance and leasing brokerage via equipment-vendor (dealer) programs
subindustry: Small-ticket and middle-ticket equipment finance/lease brokerage ($10k-$500k)
product_service: Point-of-sale financing desk for equipment dealers (restaurant, medical/dental, construction, printing, fitness, trucks) plus direct-to-business lease/loan placement with a panel of funders.
target_customer: Equipment dealers/vendors (channel) and the small businesses buying from them.
purchase_motivation: Dealers close more sales when financing is instant; buyers preserve cash and get Section 179-friendly structures.
spending_evidence: ELFA describes a $1.5T U.S. equipment finance industry and ~$140B 2026 new-deal activity per its CAPEX Finance Index headline [C, WS01-S036]; NEFA membership explicitly includes commercial finance brokers [D, WS01-S037]; National Funding runs an equipment-vendor program [D, WS01-S026].
representative_operators: NEFA member brokers (names not verified) [D, WS01-S037]
National Funding — equipment financing 2-5 yr terms, vendor program [D, WS01-S026]
revenue_mechanism: Funder-paid points/spread on funded deals (broker 'buys' a rate and sells to client within funder limits) and documentation fees; levels unpublished in sources reviewed.
typical_transaction_value: $60k lease x ~3-6 points = ~$1.8k-$3.6k per deal [E — points range unverified]
direct_costs: Dealer referral spiffs, rep commissions, credit pulls/data.
contribution_profit_note: ~$1.5-3k per funded deal [E]; vendor programs can produce steady monthly flow.
working_capital_note: Paid by funder at/after funding; no balance-sheet exposure in pure brokerage.
sales_cycle: Dealer onboarding 1-3 months; individual deals 3-15 days.
repeat_purchase: recurring — dealers send repeat flow; end customers return for additional equipment.
acquisition_channels: Direct outreach to independent equipment dealers (identifiable via manufacturer dealer locators)
customer_accessibility: Dealers are numerous, publicly listed and feel financing pain; banks and captive finance arms compete.
supplier_accessibility: Assumed: many independent lessors/banks accept broker paper (NEFA ecosystem) [D, WS01-S037]; specific funder broker requirements (years in business, volume) not verified.
